name: Law Firm (Private Practice)
description: Traditional private practice law firm organized as a partnership. Built on a strict hierarchy: Equity Partners, Non-Equity Partners, Senior Associates, Associates, Paralegals, and Legal Assistants. Practice groups are organized by specialization (corporate, litigation, IP, real estate, etc.) with a Managing Partner and Executive Committee providing firm-wide governance. Compensation and advancement are driven by billable hours, origination, and book of business.

org_structure.overview: Law firms in private practice follow a partnership model with a clear hierarchy based on experience, billable hours, and business origination. At the top, equity partners own the firm and share profits. Non-equity partners (income partners) are salaried senior lawyers on track to equity or serving as permanent senior associates. Associates are salaried lawyers working toward partnership, typically in a structured 6-10 year track. Paralegals and legal assistants provide critical support, often specializing in specific practice areas. The firm is governed by a Managing Partner and Executive Committee who handle strategic direction, while practice group leaders manage day-to-day operations within their specialties. Billable hour targets, origination credit, and realization rates drive compensation and advancement.

departments.name: Firm Governance & Executive
departments.description: Highest leadership level responsible for firm strategy, financial performance, partner compensation, risk management, and firm-wide policy. Sets the vision and manages the business of the firm.

roles.title: Managing Partner / Chair
roles.description: Senior executive elected by partners to lead the firm; sets strategic direction, manages firm finances, oversees partner compensation, and represents the firm externally.

roles.title: Executive Committee Member
roles.description: Elected partners who serve as the firm's governing board; makes major decisions on strategy, compensation, partner admissions, and firm policy.

roles.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
roles.description: Non-lawyer senior executive responsible for firm operations: finance, HR, IT, facilities, marketing, and practice management.

roles.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
roles.description: Manages firm financials: revenue forecasting, billing and collections, partner compensation calculations, budgeting, and financial reporting.

roles.title: General Counsel (Firm)
roles.description: In-house lawyer advising the firm on ethics, conflicts of interest, risk management, professional liability, and regulatory compliance.

departments.name: Partners
departments.description: Licensed attorneys who are owners (equity) or senior salaried (non-equity) members of the firm. Partners originate business, lead client relationships, supervise matters, and mentor junior lawyers. Equity partners share firm profits; non-equity partners receive a salary plus bonus.

roles.title: Equity Partner
roles.description: Owner of the firm; shares in profits, originates business, leads client relationships, supervises matters, and participates in firm governance. Highest rank in the firm.

roles.title: Non-Equity / Income Partner
roles.description: Senior salaried attorney with partnership title but no ownership stake; typically on track for equity or serving a permanent senior role. May originate business and lead matters.

roles.title: Of Counsel
roles.description: Senior attorney with specialized expertise; not on partnership track. Serves in an advisory capacity, often on complex matters, transitions, or specific practice niches.

roles.title: Practice Group Leader
roles.description: Partner responsible for a specific practice area (e.g., Corporate, Litigation); manages group strategy, attorney deployment, business development, and professional development within the practice.

departments.name: Associates
departments.description: Salaried attorneys working toward partnership. Organized by class year (first-year through senior). Expected to bill a target number of hours annually, develop legal skills, and build client relationships. Evaluated annually for advancement.

roles.title: Senior Associate / Supervising Associate
roles.description: Most senior associate level; manages complex matters independently, supervises junior associates, has significant client contact, and is actively considered for partnership.

roles.title: Mid-Level Associate
roles.description: Typically 3-5 years in; handles matters with substantial independence, manages discovery and drafting, and begins developing a practice niche.

roles.title: Junior Associate
roles.description: Typically 1-3 years in; performs legal research, drafts motions and briefs, handles document review, conducts due diligence, and supports senior team members.

roles.title: First-Year Associate
roles.description: Newly barred attorney in first year; participates in training rotations, basic research, drafting, and learns firm practice under close supervision.

roles.title: Summer Associate
roles.description: Law student in summer program; works on projects across practice groups, evaluated for post-graduation associate offer. Temporary position.

departments.name: Practice Groups
departments.description: Specialized legal practice areas organized as semi-autonomous groups within the firm. Each group has a leader (partner), dedicated associates, and support staff. Common groups include Corporate, Litigation, IP, Real Estate, Tax, Employment, and Trusts & Estates.

roles.title: Corporate Practice Group
roles.description: Handles M&A, venture capital, private equity, securities, corporate governance, and general business counseling. May include sub-specialties.

roles.title: Litigation Practice Group
roles.description: Handles civil litigation, trials, appeals, arbitration, and dispute resolution across practice areas. Includes specialized sub-groups (commercial, product liability, white collar).

roles.title: Intellectual Property Group
roles.description: Handles patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, IP litigation, patent prosecution, and IP licensing.

roles.title: Real Estate Group
roles.description: Handles real estate transactions, development, leasing, finance, land use, and zoning matters.

roles.title: Tax & Estates Group
roles.description: Handles tax planning, tax controversy, estate planning, trust administration, and wealth management for high-net-worth individuals and businesses.

departments.name: Paralegals & Legal Support
departments.description: Non-lawyer professionals who provide essential legal support under attorney supervision. Paralegals handle document management, due diligence, filings, and case coordination. Often specialized by practice group.

roles.title: Senior Paralegal / Paralegal Manager
roles.description: Most experienced paralegals; manage complex document projects, supervise junior paralegals, and handle specialized tasks like trial preparation or due diligence management.

roles.title: Paralegal / Legal Assistant
roles.description: Prepares and files legal documents, manages discovery, conducts factual research, organizes case files, drafts correspondence, and assists with trial preparation.

roles.title: Junior Paralegal
roles.description: Supports senior paralegals with document review, filing, database management, and administrative legal tasks.

roles.title: Docketing / Calendar Clerk
roles.description: Manages court deadlines, filing calendars, scheduling, and docketing for litigation and transactional matters.

roles.title: Document Review Attorney
roles.description: Contract attorney reviewing documents in discovery for privilege, relevance, and confidentiality. Often project-based.

departments.name: Firm Operations / Business Services
departments.description: Non-legal professional staff who run the business operations of the firm: finance, HR, IT, marketing, facilities, and knowledge management.

roles.title: Finance Director / Controller
roles.description: Manages billing, collections, accounts payable, trust accounting, and financial reporting. Ensures compliance with bar trust accounting rules.

roles.title: Billing Specialist
roles.description: Prepares and sends client invoices, processes billing adjustments, manages e-billing portals, and follows up on accounts receivable.

roles.title: HR Director
roles.description: Manages attorney and staff recruitment, benefits, performance management, professional development, diversity initiatives, and employee relations.

roles.title: HR Coordinator / Recruiter
roles.description: Coordinates recruiting, onboards new hires, manages summer associate programs, and supports performance review processes.

roles.title: IT Director / CIO
roles.description: Manages technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, practice management software, document management systems, and IT support.

roles.title: IT Support Specialist
roles.description: Provides desktop support, manages user accounts, troubleshoots software and hardware issues, and supports remote access.

roles.title: Marketing & Business Development Director
roles.description: Develops firm brand, manages website and social media, coordinates events, supports partner BD efforts, and manages PR and firm communications.

roles.title: Marketing Coordinator
roles.description: Supports marketing initiatives: event coordination, content creation, social media management, and directory submissions.

roles.title: Knowledge Management / Librarian
roles.description: Manages legal research resources, precedent libraries, practice guides, and knowledge-sharing platforms.

roles.title: Office Services / Facilities Manager
roles.description: Manues office facilities, reception, mail room, supplies, vendor relationships, and office space planning.

key_relationships: Equity Partner and their supervising associates form the core client service team; the Partner originates and oversees, associates execute, and all billable hours flow to the partner's matters.
Managing Partner and Executive Committee meet regularly to govern the firm; major decisions (compensation, partner admission, strategy) require committee approval.
Practice Group Leader coordinates with the Managing Partner on group performance, staffing, and strategic direction while managing their own associate team.
Senior Associate serves as the primary bridge between Partners and Junior Associates, reviewing work product and managing day-to-case execution.
Paralegals report to attorneys on specific matters but may have a dotted line to a Paralegal Manager for workload and professional development.
Billing Specialist works closely with assigned partners and associates to ensure timely and accurate client invoicing and collections.
Marketing Director supports each Practice Group Leader with business development initiatives, pitch materials, and market positioning.
Recruiting team partners with Practice Group Leaders to identify hiring needs and manage the associate recruiting and summer program pipeline.
IT and Knowledge Management teams support all attorneys with technology tools, research resources, and practice efficiency systems.
